core: Conditional impossibility of voluntary rights preservation if exploit truly dominates A's fully specified utility; identify which assumptions allow concern to become endogenous and stable. Stability under preferences, matching, deception, self-modification, and complexity is not universal.
version_corrections: 2023 Alger/Weibull corrects a claim of the 2016 paper already indexed in C05; NOT blanket retraction.
2026 Wang/Wu SSRN replaces rather than duplicates earlier 2023 arXiv abstract.
2019 Heller/Mohlin journal and 2020 arXiv are same study, not independent replications.
2016 Everitt Springer proceedings and arXiv 1605.03142 are one research work.
2019 Alger/Weibull synthesis cites its own 2013 and 2016 models; NOT new independent experiment.
2021 Akdeniz/van Veelen is a scholarly REVIEW not newly randomized experimental evidence.

origins.title: Evolution and Kantian morality: A correction and addendum
origins.finding: Corrects the second claim of Theorem 1 of Alger/Weibull (2016): proof presupposed nonempty relevant equilibrium/best-response sets although stated assumptions did not guarantee that; proves instability of competing functions under stronger conditions, retaining the first statement on the specified Homo moralis evolutionary stability.
origins.counter: NOT a wholesale retraction of the 2016 stability statement. A sufficient condition under specific assumptions cannot guarantee universal other-autonomy protection or dynamic matching conditions.
origins.original_prior_relation: C05 previously includes original Alger/Weibull 2016 doi:10.1016/j.geb.2016.05.006; link this erratum. The 2023 Toulouse draft is the SAME correction, not an additional source.

origins.title: Coevolution of deception and preferences: Darwin and Nash meet Machiavelli
origins.finding: Preferences and ability to deceive coevolve; efficient outcomes stable under modeled conditional observability and deception costs, with additional criterion comparing deviation gain and effective deception cost.
origins.counter: Material efficiency is NOT same as preserving independently goal-directed B, and deception can mimic prosocial preferences. 2020 arXiv version and earlier papers are not fresh independent samples. Abstract-level theorem summary; not verified proof derivation.
origins.original_prior_relation: New cycle DOI, but prior general observability literature Dekel/Ely/Yilankaya C05 precedes it.

origins.title: Preference Evolution under Partner Choice
origins.finding: Revised Aug 16 2026: preference evolution with endogenous stable matching and correlated equilibrium may favor partly efficient self-protecting preferences; under incomplete information parochial (in-group-favoring) type stands out by inducing sorting.
origins.counter: Efficient cooperation among chosen partners may coexist with neglect of outsiders/expendable B. Unpublished 2026 model, not original AI experiment; 2023 arXiv:2304.11504 is an earlier VERSION and differs in detail, avoid treating its abstract as current exact result.
origins.original_prior_relation: 2023 arXiv 2304.11504 same work as 2026 SSRN revision; stable identity DOI SSRN only.

origins.authors: Anthony DiGiovanni; Nicolas Macé; Jesse Clifton
origins.title: Evolutionary Stability of Other-Regarding Preferences Under Complexity Costs
origins.finding: Expanding strategy choice to include fixed actions can undermine unique evolutionary stability of other-regarding utility preferences; costly context-specific rules across multiple interactions can restore conditional stability of subjective other-regarding decision making.
origins.counter: Complexity costs and distribution over many contexts are decisive assumptions; theory allows altruism or spite, not guaranteed outsider-autonomy. Do not claim actual advanced AI would face these costs. The arXiv and Learning Evolution Games conference are one work.
origins.original_prior_relation: Related original 2007 Dekel/Ely/Yilankaya C05 and original Alger/Weibull C01/C05; not a new empirical sample.

origins.authors: Tom Everitt; Daniel Filan; Mayank Daswani; Marcus Hutter
origins.title: Self-Modification of Policy and Utility Function in Rational Agents
origins.finding: Formal RL self-modification model: under specified assumptions, self-modification is innocuous iff a value function correctly anticipates changes and evaluates future with current utility function; also characterizes failure modes of naive goal preservation.
origins.counter: Conditional theorem is NOT evidence a real AI optimizes those functions, that goals necessarily remain constant, or that other agents are included in the original utility. 2016 arXiv and Springer conference are one study.
origins.original_prior_relation: New specific self-modification theory reference, concept overlaps C05 endogenous preference and C14 toy model.

origins.title: The evolution of morality and the role of commitment
origins.finding: Reviews a commitment mechanism that can explain prosocial commitments along with anger, revenge, refusal and strategically disadvantageous choices; commitment need not require repeated interaction or population structure in presented game scenarios.
origins.counter: Morality can sustain coercive retaliation as well as generosity; no universal implication that a dominant agent preserves another's independent existence. It is a review/argument using models and existing evidence, not newly collected experiment.
origins.original_prior_relation: Directly cautions against assuming commitment always delivers non-domination; does not re-count related Güth ultimatum original.

origins.title: Evolutionary Models of Preference Formation
origins.finding: Review distinguishes large well-mixed populations with privately held preferences (often favoring material selfishness) from assortative matching/observable preference models where Kantian concern may become advantageous.
origins.counter: This review is not independent corroborating empirical evidence for 2013 Alger/Weibull; it summarizes same theory lineage; assumptions about interactions and observation are not guarantees about all outsider entities.
origins.original_prior_relation: Cross-cites C01 Homo Moralis, C05 evolution of preferences; literature review not separate sample.

origins.title: Consistent conjectures and the evolutionary stability of other-regarding preferences
origins.finding: Under consistent conjectures, stable other-regarding preference approaches zero in the large finite population limit; under zero conjectures the direction can depend on strategic complementarity.
origins.counter: DOI/title/model outcome verified from publisher original, authors not independently verified in this turn; retain UNKNOWN rather than invent. Non-observed economy and abstract-only proof scope.
origins.original_prior_relation: Potential disconfirming boundary to universal evolutionary selection of altruism; no data collected by PI.

epistemic_constraint: Publisher abstract/institution record/HTML where accessible; not all theorem proofs were verified. No actual independent AI rights or free-exit human test is claimed.
